title: Safe refrigerator and freezer outage log
summary: Preserve cold by keeping doors closed and record outage time and temperature evidence before deciding what food or medicine can be used.
content: Action sequence: Write the exact time power failed and avoid opening appliance doors merely to check. Record any thermometer reading, door opening, generator transfer, restored-power time, and official food or medicine advice. Separate decisions for food, refrigerated medicine, breast milk, and other temperature-sensitive items. Label uncertain items and obtain authoritative guidance before use; discard items that are officially considered unsafe. Safety boundary: Do not taste food to judge safety. Do not apply general food timing rules to medicines; obtain product-specific advice.
steps: Write the exact time power failed and avoid opening appliance doors merely to check.
warnings: Do not taste food to judge safety.
common_mistakes: Do not taste food to judge safety.

title: Carbon monoxide prevention during an outage
summary: Prevent invisible carbon monoxide buildup by keeping all fuel-burning devices outdoors and away from occupied openings.
content: Action sequence: Use generators, grills, charcoal, pressure washers, and other fuel-burning engines outdoors only and far from doors, windows, and vents. Point exhaust away from occupied areas and prevent rain exposure without enclosing the engine. Test carbon-monoxide alarms and move everyone to fresh air immediately if an alarm sounds or symptoms such as headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea, chest pain, or confusion appear. Call 112 from a safe outdoor location and do not re-enter until professionals say it is safe. Safety boundary: Never use a gas oven or stovetop to heat the home. Never run a generator in a home, garage, basement, balcony enclosure, shed attached to the home, or near occupied openings.

warnings: Never use a gas oven or stovetop to heat the home.

title: Utility shutoff identification without unsafe operation
summary: Label water, electricity, gas, and fuel controls and define who may operate them so an emergency does not become a live-utility accident.
content: Action sequence: Photograph and sketch each main control, meter, access route, tool requirement, and provider emergency number. Ask qualified providers which controls a resident may safely operate and which require a professional. Keep the access area dry, clear, lit, and free from stored objects. After any shutoff, label who acted, why, when, and who must inspect before restart. Safety boundary: Do not touch wet, damaged, sparking, hot, gas-affected, or unknown utility equipment. Do not restore gas or electricity after damage without the required qualified inspection.
steps: Photograph and sketch each main control, meter, access route, tool requirement, and provider emergency number.
warnings: Do not touch wet, damaged, sparking, hot, gas-affected, or unknown utility equipment.

title: Apartment stairwell emergency inspection from a safe position
summary: Check whether the normal exit has smoke, heat, water, debris, structural damage, or crowding before committing the household to it.
content: Action sequence: From the protected side, look, listen, and smell for smoke, heat, gas, water, falling material, alarms, and people moving. Test a door for unusual heat without opening into a suspected fire and keep the household behind the safe boundary. Use the stairs only when they are clear and authorities have not restricted them; never rely on a lift during fire. If the route is unsafe, close the boundary, call 112, give the floor and apartment, and move to the planned protected waiting location. Safety boundary: Do not open a door into visible smoke, strong heat, or suspected fire. Do not enter a damaged stairwell to retrieve property or check another floor.
steps: From the protected side, look, listen, and smell for smoke, heat, gas, water, falling material, alarms, and people moving.
warnings: Do not open a door into visible smoke, strong heat, or suspected fire.

title: Battery charging priority board during long outages
summary: Allocate limited charging to emergency communication, medical needs, lighting, and verified information before entertainment or convenience.
content: Action sequence: List every device, owner, purpose, current charge, minimum safe reserve, charging time, and compatible source. Rank life-sustaining medical devices and 112 communication first, followed by lighting, radio, navigation, and household coordination. Use scheduled charging windows and airplane or low-power modes outside those windows. Inspect for swelling, leakage, heat, odour, damaged cables, or wet connectors before each charge. Safety boundary: Do not charge a damaged, wet, swollen, leaking, or unusually hot battery. Do not connect unknown adapters or overload an improvised power source.
steps: List every device, owner, purpose, current charge, minimum safe reserve, charging time, and compatible source.
warnings: Do not charge a damaged, wet, swollen, leaking, or unusually hot battery.
